info.blurb: The Sun is a G2V yellow dwarf at the centre of the Solar System, holding 99.86% of its mass. Its core fuses hydrogen into helium, releasing the light and heat that sustain Earth.
info.funFact: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach Earth.

info.blurb: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun, a cratered, airless world that swings between scorching days and freezing nights.
info.funFact: One Mercury day, sunrise to sunrise, lasts about 176 Earth days.

info.blurb: Venus is Earth's near-twin in size, wrapped in a crushing carbon-dioxide atmosphere and clouds of sulphuric acid. A runaway greenhouse keeps its surface near 464 C.
info.funFact: Venus spins backwards, and its day is longer than its year.

info.blurb: Earth is the third planet and the only world known to host life, with liquid water covering about 71% of its surface and a protective magnetic field.
info.funFact: Earth is the densest planet in the Solar System.

info.blurb: Mars is a cold desert world with rusty soil, the tallest volcano in the Solar System and a canyon system that dwarfs any on Earth.
info.funFact: Olympus Mons rises about two and a half times the height of Mount Everest.

info.blurb: Jupiter is the largest planet, a gas giant more massive than all the other planets combined. Its Great Red Spot is a storm wider than Earth.
info.funFact: Jupiter spins faster than any other planet; its day lasts under 10 hours.

info.blurb: Saturn is a gas giant famous for its dazzling rings of ice and rock. It is the least dense planet, with an average density less than that of water.
info.funFact: Its glorious rings are enormous but only tens of metres thick in places.

info.blurb: Uranus is an ice giant that orbits tipped on its side, probably after a giant impact, so it rolls around the Sun. Methane gives it a pale blue-green colour.
info.funFact: Its extreme tilt gives each pole about 42 years of continuous sunlight.

info.blurb: Neptune is the farthest planet, a windy ice giant where supersonic storms rage. It was the first planet found by mathematical prediction rather than by chance.
info.funFact: Its winds are the fastest in the Solar System, exceeding 2,000 km/h.

info.blurb: Pluto is a small icy dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt with five known moons. New Horizons revealed nitrogen-ice plains and mountains of water ice.
info.funFact: Pluto is smaller than Earth's Moon.

info.blurb: Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt and the only dwarf planet in the inner Solar System, with bright salt deposits and possible water ice.
info.funFact: It contains roughly a quarter of the asteroid belt's total mass.

info.blurb: Eris is a dwarf planet far beyond Neptune and slightly more massive than Pluto; its discovery led astronomers to redefine what a planet is.
info.funFact: Its 2005 discovery prompted the new definition of a planet.

info.blurb: Haumea is a fast-spinning dwarf planet stretched into an oval by its rapid rotation, and it has a ring and two small moons.
info.funFact: A day on Haumea lasts under four hours, among the fastest known.

info.blurb: Makemake is a bright dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt, reddish like Pluto and coated in frozen methane.
info.funFact: Discovered just after Easter 2005, it was named for the creator god of Easter Island.

info.blurb: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite, stabilising our planet's axial tilt and driving the ocean tides.
info.funFact: It is slowly drifting away from Earth by about 3.8 cm per year.

info.blurb: Phobos is the larger, inner moon of Mars, a dark, cratered body spiralling slowly inward toward the planet.
info.funFact: It rises in the west and sets in the east, twice every Martian day.

info.blurb: Deimos is the smaller, outer moon of Mars, a lumpy grey body only about 12 km across.
info.funFact: It is so small that from Mars it would look like a bright star.

info.blurb: Io is the most volcanically active world in the Solar System, squeezed by Jupiter's tides into constant eruptions of sulphur.
info.funFact: Hundreds of active volcanoes paint Io in vivid yellow and red.

info.blurb: Europa is an icy moon of Jupiter with a possible global ocean beneath its frozen shell, one of the best places to search for life.
info.funFact: Its ice crust may hide twice as much water as all of Earth's oceans.

info.blurb: Ganymede is the largest moon in the Solar System, bigger than Mercury, and the only moon known to generate its own magnetic field.
info.funFact: It is larger than the planet Mercury.

info.blurb: Callisto is an ancient, heavily cratered moon of Jupiter whose surface has barely changed in billions of years.
info.funFact: It has the oldest, most cratered surface known in the Solar System.

info.blurb: Titan is Saturn's largest moon, the only moon with a thick atmosphere, and the only other world with rivers and seas on its surface.
info.funFact: Its rivers and seas are made of liquid methane, not water.

info.blurb: Enceladus is a small, bright moon of Saturn that vents plumes of water vapour and ice from a hidden subsurface ocean.
info.funFact: Its icy plumes feed one of Saturn's faint outer rings.

info.blurb: Rhea is Saturn's second-largest moon, an icy, cratered world that may even have a thin ring of its own.
info.funFact: It may be the only moon known to have its own ring system.

info.blurb: Titania is the largest moon of Uranus, an icy world scarred by enormous canyons formed as it expanded and cracked.
info.funFact: Its canyons stretch for more than a thousand kilometres.

info.blurb: Oberon is the outermost large moon of Uranus, an ancient icy body with dark deposits scattered across its cratered face.
info.funFact: It is the second-largest moon of Uranus and unusually dark.

info.blurb: Triton is Neptune's largest moon and orbits backwards, suggesting it was captured from the Kuiper Belt. Ice geysers erupt from its surface.
info.funFact: It is one of the few geologically active moons known.

info.blurb: Charon is Pluto's largest moon, so large that the two orbit a point in space between them, making them almost a double dwarf planet.
info.funFact: Pluto and Charon are sometimes described as a double planet.
